summary: Observe host resource lanes with separate admission, execution and retirement clocks

replay.detail: Telemetry hooks consume the host authority's reconciled state; no replay or projection changes.

schema.detail: Membership bodies gain optional retirementRequestedAt, persisted before OS teardown, and clockEpoch/clockUncertain recovery evidence. Existing authoritative records retain custody and decode absent clock fields as unknown; recovery reports uncertainty rather than fabricating a historical retirement start or granting a fresh timeout budget.

rules.detail: Observations never grant admission, resolve holds, or release physical custody.

compatibility.detail: Adds st.resource.admission, st.resource.execution and st.resource.release INTERNAL root spans linked to run/attempt traces, plus structured resource.lane.phase logs. Adds st.resource.occupancy, st.resource.queue and st.resource.holds observable gauges, and st.resource.wait.duration, st.resource.execution.duration, st.resource.release.duration and st.resource.hold.duration histograms in seconds. Configured lane is the only identity dimension on metrics; phase histograms also have bounded outcome. Run, step, attempt, membership, generation and invocation remain on traces/logs only.

downtime.detail: Normal binary rollout; no telemetry backfill.

manual.detail: Uses existing independent OTLP signal configuration and exporter providers. Native lane spans capture OpenTelemetry contexts directly, independently of program-attempt trace serialization. Native finite launches take a typed authorization request grouping lane policy, membership binding, current-owner guard and payload-release authorization.

recovery.detail: Recovery recreates only live observation segments with explicit clock uncertainty and persisted prior elapsed age; completed histogram samples are not replayed. Older readers ignore the additive retirement clock field; ordinary binary rollback retains custody records.
